title: Rotary Offset on the Tormach microARC 4: every level that cuts takes two laps of A, so the PathPilot post refuses it (A counts past the -360..360 travel)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (stacked on PR #2342, which posts wrapped A on `tormach.cps`).

**What happens.** A Rotary Offset rough on the microARC 4 machine file does not post once a level meets the part:

```
post blocked - 1 warning(s): A361.862 in operation Journal is beyond the A axis travel -360..360 degrees - A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over), so the operation turns too far in one direction
```

**Why.** `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_offset.rs` develops the bar as a cover of two laps plus the seam pad ("the cover is two laps, the seam copy included"); only an air level sweeps one lap. PathPilot does not roll A over (Hub reading 1 on #796), so the post counts A on, and the machine file states A travel -360..360 (kept in PR #2342: "PathPilot's real A limits are an open Hub check"). Two laps plus the pad cannot fit in 720 degrees.

**Repro (on the #1904 branch, before the demo was changed to Rotary Parallel).** 3/4 in round bar as stock (a model, R 0.375 in, X-1.5..0), a stepped model (journal R 0.340 in), 1/8 in ball, Rotary Offset with radial stepdown 0.03 in, any strategy (Auto, Zigzag, Waterline, Offset rings; climb or conventional): each is refused with A between 360.9 and 363.4. With a Box stock and a 0.1 in stepdown the only level is an air level (one lap, A-86.25..273.75) and it posts, but it cuts nothing.

**Expected.** One of:
- the rough's rings close without a second lap (or each ring unwinds: lift, turn A back, go on), so a level stays inside 720 degrees; or
- the machine file states the travel PathPilot really allows, if the Hub check of PR #2342 (step 5) shows it is wider; or
- the refusal says what to change.

**Workaround.** None found: Rotary Offset cannot be used on this machine file today. Rotary Parallel posts (its A stays inside one turn).

Done means: a Rotary Offset rough of a round bar posts on `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` with `tormach.cps`, pinned by a test, or the limit is documented with a refusal that names the fix.

title: Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model to the axis: on a bar held in a chuck that is a cut through the bar, and no setting limits it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, stacked on PR #2342).

**What happens.** Rotary Parallel lays the bar down and runs the finishing raster over the whole model, end faces included (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`, `rotary_parallel`). Each end face is finished down to the fitted axis. On rotary work the bar is held at one end (chuck) or both (chuck and centre), so the chuck-side "end face" of the model is inside solid bar. The pass there is a groove one tool diameter wide, cut from the skin to the centreline: it parts the bar.

**Evidence.** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` on the #1904 branch: a cylinder model 0.680 in across from X-1.25 to X0, a Box stock from X-2 to X0, a 1/8 in ball tool. The posted program (`examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`) feeds the tool tip at X-1.3125 down to Z-0.029 (Z is the radius from the A centreline), with the stock box going on to X-2. Pinned by `continuous_4axis_part::the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`.

What stops it today, and what does not:
- A tool whose flute is shorter than the depth is blocked at post: "shank/holder at move N collides with the uncut stock" (pinned by `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`, 1/2 in flute). Good.
- A tool with a long enough flute (5/8 in here, or the catalog `BN-0600` default of 15 mm) posts with no warning.
- No setting keeps the pass off an end face. **Bottom Z** is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius: at 0 it keeps only the half of the bar within about 81 degrees of the top and still cuts the end faces to the axis. **Top Z** / **Clearance Z** are radii for the links. There is no axial window (Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset read heights as stations; on a bar lying flat those are inert).
- The kit golden of PR #2342 (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) has the same shape: its stock ends where its model ends, so CamCraft sees air where the real bar goes on into the jaws.

**Expected.** A way to finish the turned surface only: an axial window (from/to stations along the fitted axis), or an option to leave the end faces, so the pass stops at a shoulder. Until then, a named warning or refusal when an end-face pass enters stock that goes on past the end of the model.

**Workaround.** None for a real cut on a held bar. The #1904 guide page runs the program as an air cut only and says why.

Priority note: filed as P3 (wrong behaviour with no silent gouge of the part: the stock is cut, the model is not). The maintainer may read "parts the bar off with no warning" as P1.

Done means: a Rotary Parallel job on a bar that goes on past the model's chuck-side end either leaves that end face alone by a setting, or is refused or warned by name; a test pins it; the #1904 guide page drops its "air cut only" limit.

title: Bore contour: a linear lead with a Ramp entry under carried stock gives RapidInStock on the second level

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A bore-side contour (`Side::Inside`) has carried stock over Top Z (#1559, `Approach::material_top`). It uses `Lead::Linear { length: 2.0 }` and `Entry3D::Ramp`, with `Links::PLANAR` or with the level link `Link::Retract`. Verify with the stock top at the carried stock gives `RapidInStock` on the descent into the second level.

Reproduction (motion crate, the fixture of `crates/motion/tests/one_descent.rs`):
- hole: a circle of radius 10, tool diameter 6, Top Z 0, Bottom Z -6, stepdown 2;
- `links.approach.material_top = Some(5.0)`;
- verify with `stock_top_z: 5.0`, `Mode::Area`.

Result: `verify [RapidInStock { at: 2673 }]`. Move 2673 is the rapid from Z 25 to Z 2.0 at (0.232, -6.546). Move 2674 is the substituted axial dive from Z 2 to Z -2 (note "the ramp's chord is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead").

`main` at `fac6c8e8d` gives the same result. PR #2013 does not change it.

## What is not known

A probe found each footprint point of that rapid within 2.87 mm of a planar feed at Z 0 that comes before it (tool radius 3). Thus the rapid can be a false conviction of the verify column law. It can also be a real rapid into a cusp of carried stock. In the application the verify warning blocks the post, so the output is not silent. This issue must find which of the two it is.

## Done means

- The cause is known: the verify reading or the dive start.
- The fix removes the warning or makes the dive start over the stock.
- The case `carried bore lead linear Ramp planar/retract` in `the_bore_contour_under_carried_stock_never_rapids_into_it` (`crates/motion/tests/one_descent.rs`, PR #2013) is no longer skipped.

title: 2D Adaptive: only the first region gets the helix entry; each other entry is a straight plunge into material, with no warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16, with two screenshots (build `v0.22.0 · f6c7f605`, a local test build):

> "Bug in 2D Adapive. This was generated by setting a stock boundary and picking the outside edge of the part. I will helix down the first hole and clearing it out all the other Entrys inside and outside the part is missing lead ins of same helix setting. Same issue if i remove the boundary.. Only a helix leadin on the first pocket.. not the secondd one. This kinda comes back to how containment is getting interpreted... But problem ppeprsista even if i pick two inside faces of the pockets.. Helix is only on the first pocket, second is justa straight plunge into the material with no warning."

What happens:

- Project `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`), 2D Adaptive, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (8 mm end mill), post Fanuc (built-in).
- Lead in / Lead out page: Entry Type `Helix`, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Minimum radius, pitch and angle on Auto, Plunge enabled.
- The operation generates: "8832 moves (27 plunge(s) @ 300, 3 level(s), 2286 arc(s)), 12 warning(s)".
- The first pocket gets the helix entry. Each other entry, inside and outside the part, is a straight plunge into the material.
- No warning names the plunges.
- The result is the same for three selections: stock boundary with the outside edge; no boundary; the two inside faces of the pockets.

Expected:

- Each entry into material uses the selected entry type (helix), at each region and each level.
- Where the helix does not fit, the ramp comes next. A straight plunge into material is the last fallback only.
- Each entry that falls back gets a warning that names the region, the level and the reason. The page says "where the helix cannot fit, a ramp and then a plunge stand in": the user must see when this happens.
- A plunge into material with a tool that cannot cut at its centre is refused or blocks the post, by the rule that the project has for such tools.
- A plunge in open air (outside the stock, or in an area that an earlier pass cleared) needs no helix and no warning.

To find:

1. Why the entry planner gives the helix to the first region only. Does it try the helix for each region, or one time for the operation?
2. If the 27 plunges are in material or in cleared area, by the stock state at that moment.
3. If the Offset rings fallback is the cause. The status line says "the HSM plan is refused: the area is a channel 10.6 mm wide ..."; the fallback path possibly does not apply the entry settings.
4. Why no warning is made.

Safety: a straight plunge into uncut material without a warning is wrong output that can break a tool. The fix changes posted G-code of 2D Adaptive (entry moves) and is under the safety floor. The verify check and the post gate do not become weaker. No real control run exists.

Related: #2232 (containment Outside, option 1 selected), and the "feed moves cross in XY at shared depth" warnings on this project (seen in the review of PR #2214).

Done means: a test on a part with two separate pockets (and one with an outside region) asserts a helix or ramp entry at each region and level where it fits, and a named warning for each entry that falls back to a plunge in material. The goldens that change are named in the PR.

title: Debug info: log the frame rate when it changes, and make the debug info panel dockable

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16. The maintainer set the priority `P2` in his own words:

> "Issue; p2; Log framerate to debug info as a value when it changes in performance once - and if it keeps jumping around log just every 10s or something like that.. Make debug info "dockable" as well."

Wanted, part 1 - frame rate in the debug info:

- The debug info shows the frame rate (and the frame time in ms) as a value.
- When the frame rate changes to a different level, the debug info logs one line with the new value. Use a threshold, so that small noise logs nothing.
- When the frame rate does not become stable, the debug info logs at most one line each 10 s. That line gives the minimum, the maximum and the mean of the interval.
- An idle application that does not repaint logs nothing.

Wanted, part 2 - dockable debug info:

- The user can dock the debug info panel as the other panels dock, and can undock it again.
- The dock position is part of the saved layout.

Rules:

- The measurement costs no work in proportion to the model. It reads the frame times that the application has (frame cost rule, #2238). The log does not request a repaint.
- The log rate limit applies to the `gpu: slow frame` lines too, or the issue says why not.
- Panel layout is ephemeral UI state, not a command.
- The text is plain English.

Done means: a unit test pins the log rule (one line for one level change; no more than one line each 10 s when the value moves; no line when idle); a structural test pins that the debug info panel is present docked and undocked; the PR has before and after screenshots.

title: Frame cost: calculate before and cache through the full application, redraw only on a change

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16:

> "caching to not have to redraw things should prob. be a strategy thru out the application to keep framerates stable and enough compute lefter over for things that matter.. Precalculation and cache is not something that will give us a penalty.. this is not game engine"

and, for the frame time: "the performance needs to gget down under 10ms to be useable".

What is wanted: one strategy for the full application. A frame does not calculate again what did not change. Derived data (chains, stitched rings, overlay geometry, panel rows, meshes, simulation views) is calculated one time, stored, and made invalid by a change of its inputs. A wait for a calculation before the display is acceptable.

Today: #2201, #2209 and #2235 each repair one place where a frame does work in proportion to the model or the selection. Each repair has its own cache and its own invalidation rule.

Work, in this order:

1. Measure. List the work that each frame does in `commands`, `scene` and `ui` on a large model (`fig8.step` and one larger), with a probe that stays in the test suite.
2. Design one cache rule: the key (a model revision, a selection revision, a document revision), who makes an entry invalid, and where the entries are stored (app layer, not UI widgets). Record it in `docs/decisions/` and in `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`.
3. Idle frames: when no input and no change exists, the app does not repaint, or it repaints from stored buffers.
4. Move each measured hot path to the rule, one sub-issue for each.
5. A budget test: a frame without a change is below 10 ms on the reference models. The gate runs it.

Safety: a cache must never show or cut stale geometry. Each cache has a test that a change of its inputs makes it invalid. The verify check and the post gate read the document, not a display cache.

Done means: the decision is recorded, the budget test is in the gate, and the sub-issues for the measured hot paths are filed. #2235 gives the first cache and the first probe.

body:
Reported by a user on Discord (f1inch), relayed by the maintainer's collaborator on 2026-11-16; filed by an agent:

> "after i add a second operation after faceing the camcraft gets so damn slow that i cant work with it."

The user shared the project privately. It is not attached here.

## The project (shape only)

- Project version 61, 17 MB on disk.
- One model of about 45,000 triangles (8.4 MB of facets).
- One setup, one box stock, one tool (4 mm router bit).
- Two operations: `Face1`, then `2D Contour1`.
- Machine: a hobby router file (FoxAlien WM-3020), grblHAL post.

## Readings (headless, release build of main 3580f3888, Linux)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `open_project` | 0.1 s |
| `generate` 2D Contour1 (forced) | 1.0 s |
| `generate` Face1 (forced) | < 0.1 s |
| `verify` | 0.2 s |

So project load, generation and verification are fast. The slowness is in the windowed shell: the redraw, the scene rebuild, the toolpath or stock display, or the simulation. #164 (closed) found a similar pattern: one CPU core at 100% in the window while `camcraft-cli process` took under a second.

The project also has two problems that are not this defect:
- The model was saved before mesh fidelity was recorded (v58 or older), so the gouge check blocks the post until the model is imported again.
- `Face1` moves go outside the machine stroke (X to -47.5, Z to -4, stroke X 0..290, Z 0..70): 626 limit problems.

A large number of findings can make a UI list slow. Check if the window rebuilds or paints all 626 findings each frame.

## What is not known yet

- Which action is slow: select an operation, regenerate, rotate the view, or play the simulation.
- The user's CamCraft version, operating system and GPU (the paths suggest Linux).
- If one operation is fast and two operations are slow.

## Done means

On a fixture with the same shape (a model of about 45,000 triangles, a Face and a 2D Contour, and several hundred findings), the windowed UI stays responsive: a frame cost close to the one-operation case, no CPU core held at 100% when idle. A test pins the cost that caused it (for example the scene or findings rebuild count for each frame).

title: Simulation: calculate the stock removal before playback, so that the animation does not lag behind the tool

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16:

> issue enhancement; all the "voxel animation" should not be realtime, it should be pre-calculation so it doesnt lag behind while playing the simulation.

What happens now:

- The simulation calculates the stock removal while the playback runs.
- On a long or dense toolpath the stock picture comes later than the tool position. The animation lags.

What is wanted:

- The stock removal is calculated before the playback, not during it.
- During playback the stock picture is at the tool position at each moment, at each playback speed, and when the user moves the time slider forward or back.

Points for the design (record the choices in `docs/decisions/`):

- Where the calculation runs: a background job after generation, or at the first press of Play, with a progress display and a cancel control. The UI must not stop during it.
- What is stored: stock states at fixed steps of the program (keyframes) plus a fast replay between them, or a full list of states. Give the memory limit and what happens when a job exceeds it.
- When the stored result becomes invalid: an edit of the operation, the tool, the stock, the fixture or the setup. Use the same stamp that the operation cache uses, so that an old stock picture is never shown for a new toolpath.
- The result is ephemeral UI state. It does not go into the project file and it is not a command.
- All resources of an operation are freed when the operation is deleted (AGENTS.md, delete hooks).
- The verify step and the checks that can block the post do not change. This work changes the display only. The PR pins that.
- Related: #2177 (traced playback refuses a rotated stock), #586 / #637 (stock on the field engine).

Done means:

- A test pins that, after the calculation, the stock state at a given program position is the same as the state that the present real-time simulation reaches there.
- A test pins that a jump of the time slider (forward and back) shows the correct stock state without a new full calculation.
- A test pins that an edit of the operation makes the stored result invalid.
- A reading on one large fixture shows the calculation time and the memory use, in the PR body.

title: Depth-stepping operations cut a first level at Top Z that removes no material

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0, with a screenshot of a 2D Adaptive operation.

His words: "a common issue i see is that the first toolpath is always ontop of the part at TopZ ... even thos stepdown states "full depth" of the cut.. technically it should just be one single toolpath right?" and "find it in all operations.. This is a high effortf, P2 bug.."

## What happens

The operation has Top Z = 13 (stock top + 1), Bottom Z = 0 and Stepdown = 50 mm. It posts two full levels: one at Z 13 and one at Z 0. The level at Top Z cuts no material. It doubles the cycle time of a one-level cut.

## Cause

The shared level law starts its list at Top Z:

```rust
// crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs, cut_levels
let mut z = top;
while z > bottom + tol {
    zs.push(z);      // the first level is `top`
    z -= stepdown;
}
zs.push(bottom);
```

`cut_levels(13, 0, 50)` gives `[13, 0]`. The correct list is `[0]`. With a stepdown of 5 it gives `[13, 8, 3, 0]`. The correct list is `[8, 3, 0]`.

`crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` `ladder_planes` restates the same law, and its unit test pins the wrong list (`ladder_planes(20.0, 0.0, 5.0) == [20, 15, 10, 5, 0]`).

## Callers found (read-only search, not complete)

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`: `adaptive_troch.rs:158`, `bore.rs:308`, `circular.rs:278` and `:280`, `contour_params.rs:216` (2D Contour), `face.rs:156`, `pocket.rs:277`, `pocket_hsm.rs:49` and `pocket_troch.rs:68` (level counts for the budget), `slots.rs:160` and `:343`, `trochoid_slot.rs:319`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs:89`, `:123`, `:236`, `:258` (3D Pocket and its rest pass)
- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:74`, `:182`, `:233` (`ladder_planes`, the 3D pocket region build)
- `crates/motion/tests/control_comp.rs` (a test helper with the same name)

Not yet read: `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ladder.rs` `levels`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs` `ladder`, `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`, the turning, drilling (peck), engraving, chamfer, plasma and EDM depth ladders, and each operation with its own loop.

## For the work

1. Audit each operation of each machine type for a level at Top Z (or at the material top) that removes no material. List each in the PR with the result.
2. Fix the shared law so that the first level is `top - stepdown`, and the last level is `bottom` exactly. Use one law: `ladder_planes` in `app` must use the motion law, or match it by a shared test.
3. Check the special cases:
   - Top Z below the stock top (material above Top Z): no level may cut more than one stepdown. Find what each operation means by Top Z, and state it.
   - `circular.rs:278` starts at a previous level (`cut_levels(prev, floor, ...)`): make sure that it does not cut the previous level two times.
   - Face: a single pass at `cut_z` stays one pass.
   - A stepdown of 0 or a span of 0: the current refusal and the one-plane result stay.
   - Rest machining and the 3D Pocket shell levels: the level count and the budget readings change. Restate the budget pins with the reason.
   - The ramp, helix and plunge entries that read `top_z` as the material top (`Motion::top_z`) must stay correct.
4. The size of the last step (the remainder or equal steps) is a separate choice. Keep the current remainder rule, and file a follow-up issue for the choice.

This changes posted G-code for existing projects (one level fewer for each depth-stepping operation). It is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- No operation posts a level at Top Z that removes no material when Top Z is at or above the material top.
- One-level case: Top Z 13, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 50 gives one level at Z 0. Pinned for 2D Adaptive, 2D Pocket, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular and 3D Pocket.
- Multi-level case: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 5 gives `[15, 10, 5, 0]`. Pinned on the shared law and on `ladder_planes`.
- Each changed golden is listed in the PR with the reason. The PR says that posted G-code changes.
- Each verify and gouge pin of the touched operations stays green.

title: finish3d: a straight link across gap openings (gap_link: Jump, Straight)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
What the user asked for (chat, 2026-11-14): "i want it to form a smooth link move over holes in the surface. lets start with a straight line between each edge of the hole. later we can add splines and curves for how to connect them."

What happens now: finish3d (Parallel and the other march patterns) breaks a raster line where the tool cannot stand, for example over a hole. The chain between the two runs lifts to the retract plane. The tool makes an air hop for every gap. On a part with many holes this is slow and the moves look wrong in the GUI.

Change: add an operation parameter `gap_link` to the finishing parameters. The parameter is a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): today's behaviour, unchanged. The chain lifts to the retract plane.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed move between the end of one run and the start of the next, at the two end points' own tip height.

Law for `Straight`: both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march construction. The author certifies the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS`. A grazing contact at the rim passes. A real bite refuses. On a refusal the chain takes the `Jump` hop. No air margin is added for `Straight`; `Jump` keeps its own retract law.

Also fixed, needed by this feature: the raster serpentine ran a broken back line wrong. It reversed only each piece's points and kept the pieces in grid order. Every gap link then jumped back across the field instead of crossing its gap. A back line now reverses whole: the pieces in reverse order, and each piece's points reversed. This also shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines.

How the parameter is stored: the project digest takes a `0x4D` tag plus a variant byte only when `gap_link` is not `Jump`. The project file grammar takes the words `jump` and `straight`. No project-file version step-up. The MCP params door and the UI combo carry the same two options.

Done means:

- The Gap link dropdown offers Jump and Straight; Jump is the default and writes the old bytes.
- Over a holed plate, `Straight` authors rim-to-rim Feed links at the run height and no retract hop for those gaps.
- A `Straight` link that would cut the part is refused, and the hop stands (Prime Directive).
- Every gap crossing on a broken back line spans one gap, never the field.
- Pins: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs`, the round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and the MCP params-door test.

body:
What happens: post-merge run 43535610115 (push to main at 745edc36a) ended with job `gate` = failure and job `report` = skipped. The rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)` was not opened or commented on.

Expected: AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": a red post-merge gate opens or comments on the rolling issue; the next green run closes it.

Cause (read from `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` on main): the `report` job has `needs: gate` and an `if:` with no status-check function:

```
if: ${{ (needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure') && needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true' && (...) }}
```

GitHub Actions adds an implicit `success()` to a job's `if` unless it contains `always()`, `failure()`, `cancelled()` or `!cancelled()`. With a failed `needs` job the implicit `success()` is false, so the job is skipped before the expression is read. The job therefore only ever runs on green.

Suggested fix: start the condition with `always() &&` (the rest already excludes cancelled and skipped runs). One line.

Note on this particular run: its only red test was `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` (`crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs`, "not within 30s"), the wall-clock flake of issue 1605, so main was not truly red here. The reporting gap is real for any failure.

A `.github/` change: the PR is read, not built, and waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`). `Process change: yes` does not apply (`.github/` is not a process file).

Found by the maintenance session while watching runs.

Done means: a post-merge run whose gate fails runs `report` and opens or comments on the rolling issue; a green run after it closes that issue; a cancelled or cut-skipped run still reports nothing.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
